cards.name: Bullet 2 - Grey
cards.summary: Symbol 'Bullet 2 - Grey' from Illustrator's Web Buttons and Bars symbol library: a round button with a pale grey outer ring and a white inner halo, a glossy silver-grey disc with a slate-grey rim, holding a bold dark-grey arrow pointing right. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 48 x 48 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: play, next and go buttons on web pages
bullet markers for lists and links
call-to-action buttons in app and banner mock-ups
avoid: a labelled button: the glyph has no text; add the label beside it with the Type tool
a flat look: the gloss and bevel are baked in; break the link and set flat fills for a flat design
cards.applies_to: the artboard of an open document: placing it creates a symbol instance, a linked copy of the symbol definition that can be moved, scaled and rotated like any object; the symbol must exist in the target document (placing from the library copies it in)
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Symbol Libraries > Web Buttons and Bars; click the symbol (it is added to the Symbols panel), then drag it onto the artboard or press Place Symbol Instance. Script: doc.symbolItems.add(doc.symbols.getByName("Bullet 2 - Grey")) in a document that holds the symbol; to use it in another document: app.open("<Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Symbols/Web Buttons and Bars.ai"), place an instance there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the symbol arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Grey-ringed white-haloed silver-grey disc with slate rim and a bold dark-grey right arrow.

Script: doc.symbolItems.add(doc.symbols.getByName("Button 1 - Blue")) in a document that holds the symbol; to use it in another document: app.open("<Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Symbols/Web Buttons and Bars.ai"), place an instance there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the symbol arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Raw render: opaque pale white-grey pill bar (mean about 233,234,235) with an outlined sky-blue play triangle at the right end; the grey 120 backing is the renderer.

review.changes: avoid: 'barely show on white (inferred)' -> reads on white only by its outline and shading, with the Button 2 - Blue thumbnail as evidence

cards.name: Button 1 - Orange
cards.summary: Symbol 'Button 1 - Orange' from Illustrator's Web Buttons and Bars symbol library: a slim, pale pill-shaped bar, white-grey with a soft top highlight and a light grey outline, with a small play triangle at its right end and no text: the triangle is a small outlined one in golden yellow with an orange outline. The thumbnail shows it on the renderer's mid-grey backing because the bar is so pale. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 173 x 29 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: search bars, link bars and call-to-action strips on web pages
text-field and menu-row backgrounds in mock-ups
slim buttons with a play or go pointer
avoid: a labelled button: the bar is blank; add the label with the Type tool
a flat look: the gloss and bevel are baked in; break the link and set flat fills for a flat design

a white background: the bar is pale white-grey and reads on white only by its thin grey outline and soft shading (the same bar is drawn on white in the Button 2 - Blue thumbnail); a coloured or grey ground shows it better
